name: Shackleton Crater Rim
description: The rim of Shackleton Crater near the lunar south pole offers near-continuous sunlight and direct line-of-sight into one of the deepest permanently shadowed regions, making it a prime candidate for Artemis III crewed exploration and volatile prospecting.

name: Malapert Massif
description: Malapert Massif is one of the tallest features near the lunar south pole, providing exceptional solar illumination and a direct Earth line-of-sight for communications. Its relatively gentle slopes make it accessible for both crewed landers and CLPS robotic missions.

name: Cabeus B Rim
description: Located on the rim of Cabeus B crater, this site is adjacent to the LCROSS impact region where water ice was confirmed. The proximity to permanently shadowed deposits and moderate solar access make it a strong candidate for in-situ resource utilization demonstrations.

name: Nobile Rim 1 (VIPER Region)
description: Nobile Rim 1 sits on the western rim of Nobile crater in the region originally targeted by the VIPER mission. It offers close access to permanently shadowed craters expected to harbor water ice, but steep local slopes present mobility challenges for rovers.

name: Apollo 11 — Mare Tranquillitatis
description: The Apollo 11 landing site in Mare Tranquillitatis serves as an equatorial baseline for comparison. The flat mare terrain provides excellent rover traversability and a predictable ~14-day sunlight / ~14-day darkness cycle, but it is far from any polar volatile deposits.
